lines.pointclick.item.rope.look: A good length of rope. Salt-stiff, but strong.
lines.pointclick.item.hook.look: An iron hook, rusty and sharp.
lines.pointclick.item.grapple.look: A hook on a rope. I could go fishing with this.
lines.pointclick.item.key.look: Morwen's brass key. It opens Finn's chain.
lines.pointclick.item.bottle.look: An empty bottle. It smells of rum.
lines.pointclick.item.oil.look: A bottle of whale oil. It smells awful.
lines.pointclick.item.matches.look: A box of matches. Five left.
lines.pointclick.tavern.notice.look.1: "WANTED: A KEEPER'S HAND FOR GULL ROCK."
lines.pointclick.tavern.notice.look.3: And a riddle, pinned up by Morwen: "UNBEATEN SINCE THE FLOOD."
lines.pointclick.lamp.log.look: The keeper's log. The last entry:
lines.pointclick.lamp.log.entry: "Oil run dry. Gone ashore for more. Back by dusk. BRAM."
lines.pointclick.dock.boat.look.free: Finn's rowboat, free of its chain.
lines.pointclick.dock.boat.look: Finn's rowboat. Chained to the post.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lamp.look.oiled: Its well is full of oil. It just needs a flame.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lamp.look: The great lamp. Its oil well is bone dry.
lines.pointclick.lamp.window.look.lit: The fleet's lanterns are turning for home!
lines.pointclick.lamp.window.look: Fog to the horizon. I can see the fleet's lanterns bobbing out there.
lines.pointclick.dock.door.look: The Salty Gull. Warm in there, and loud.
lines.pointclick.dock.rope.pickup: A good length of rope. Mine now.
lines.pointclick.dock.rope.look: A coil of rope. Nobody seems to be using it.
lines.pointclick.dock.finn.look: Finn. He's fished these waters for fifty years.
lines.pointclick.dock.finn.pickup: He's a bit big to carry.
lines.pointclick.dock.oar.look: Finn's oar, bobbing just out of reach.
lines.pointclick.dock.oar.pickup: I can't reach it from up here.
lines.pointclick.dock.chain.look: A chain and a brass padlock. Morwen's, by the look of it.
lines.pointclick.dock.gull.look: A gull. It's eyeing my sandwich. I haven't got a sandwich.
lines.pointclick.dock.gull.pickup: It would peck my eyes out.
lines.pointclick.dock.light.look: Gull Rock. Its light should be lit by now, and the fleet's out in this fog.
lines.pointclick.dock.light.use: It's miles out. I'll need a boat.
lines.pointclick.tavern.bruno.look: Bruno keeps the Salty Gull. He has arms like hams.
lines.pointclick.tavern.barrel.look: A barrel of whale oil, for the town's lamps.
lines.pointclick.tavern.barrel.use: I need something to carry it in.
lines.pointclick.tavern.barrel.open: It has a tap. I need something to carry the oil in.
lines.pointclick.tavern.barrel.pickup: It weighs more than I do.
lines.pointclick.tavern.matches.look: A box of matches on the mantel.
lines.pointclick.tavern.hook.pickup: It comes away from the rotten wood. Got it.
lines.pointclick.tavern.hook.pull: One good pull, and it comes away. Got it.
lines.pointclick.tavern.hook.look: An iron hook, screwed into rotten wood.
lines.pointclick.tavern.morwen.look: Morwen, the harbour master. Every key on the dock hangs from her belt.
lines.pointclick.tavern.bottle.pickup: An empty bottle. She won't miss it.
lines.pointclick.tavern.bottle.look: An empty bottle. Morwen's, I think.
lines.pointclick.lamp.hatch.look: A hundred and twelve steps back down to the boat.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lens.look: A great glass lens, rings inside rings. It throws the light twenty miles.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lens.use: It's the lamp inside that needs lighting.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lens.pickup: It weighs as much as a cow.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lamp.use: It needs oil, and then a flame.
lines.pointclick.lamp.lamp.open: The oil well is open. And empty.
lines.pointclick.lamp.bell.look: The fog bell. For when the light isn't enough.
lines.pointclick.lamp.can.look: The keeper's oil can. Empty, of course.
lines.pointclick.lamp.can.pickup: It's empty. No use to me.
lines.pointclick.lamp.window.open: The wind would blow the flame out.
lines.pointclick.use.rope_hook: I knot the rope to the hook. A grapple!
lines.pointclick.use.grapple_oar: Got it! I haul Finn's oar up onto the pier.
lines.pointclick.use.rope_oar: The rope just floats beside it. It needs something on the end to catch it.
lines.pointclick.use.hook_oar: My arm isn't that long. If the hook were on a line...
lines.pointclick.use.key_chain: Click! The padlock springs open, and the chain drops.
lines.pointclick.use.bottle_barrel: I fill the bottle from the tap. Whale oil. Phew.
lines.pointclick.use.oil_lamp: I pour the oil into the lamp's well. Every drop.
lines.pointclick.use.matches_lamp: There's no oil in it to burn.
lines.pointclick.use.oil_can: The lamp needs it more than the can does.
lines.pointclick.give.oar_finn: Hang on to it, Pip. You're the one rowing.
lines.pointclick.give.bottle_bruno: Fill it yourself, lad. The barrel's right there.
lines.pointclick.give.key_morwen: Keep it till the boat's back. Then I want it.
lines.pointclick.talk.intro.1: Pip! Gull Rock's gone dark. Old Bram rowed ashore for oil this morning, and he's not back.
lines.pointclick.talk.intro.2: And the whole fleet's out in this fog. Without the light they'll be on the rocks by midnight.
lines.pointclick.talk.intro.3: Then I'll light it myself! How do I get out there?
lines.pointclick.talk.intro.4: Take my rowboat, at the end of the pier. Only I dropped my oar in the drink...
lines.pointclick.talk.intro.5: And Morwen chains every boat on this dock at dusk. She's in the Salty Gull.
lines.pointclick.choice.finn.key: HOW DO I GET THE KEY?
lines.pointclick.talk.finn_oar.1: You fished it out! Good lad.
lines.pointclick.talk.finn_oar.2: Floating by the pier, just out of reach. A hook on a line would fetch it.
lines.pointclick.talk.finn_key.1: You got her to part with it? Then go!
lines.pointclick.talk.finn_key.2: Morwen won't sell it. But she can't resist a riddle contest. Never lost one, mind.
lines.pointclick.talk.finn_lamp: Oil, and a flame. Bram went ashore because the oil ran out.
lines.pointclick.talk.bruno_light: Bram's gone ashore, so the lamp's dry. You'll want oil, and a flame to put to it. There's matches on the mantel.
lines.pointclick.talk.bruno_oil: For the town's lamps, aye. Take what you need, if you've something to carry it in.
lines.pointclick.talk.bruno_morwen: Harbour master. Loves a riddle more than her own mother. Never lost a contest, she says.
lines.pointclick.talk.morwen.1: Finn's chain? Every chain on this dock is mine, Pip, and so is every key.
lines.pointclick.talk.morwen.2: But I'll give that key to anyone who beats me at riddles. Three riddles. No mistakes.
lines.pointclick.talk.riddle1: First. What has a mouth but never eats, and a bed but never sleeps?
lines.pointclick.talk.riddle2: Lucky. Second. The more of them you take, the more you leave behind.
lines.pointclick.talk.riddle3: Hmph. Last. I'm light as a feather, yet the strongest sailor can't hold me for long.
lines.pointclick.talk.won.1: Three for three! Nobody's done that since the flood.
lines.pointclick.talk.won.2: Here. Finn's padlock, and mind you bring it back.
lines.pointclick.talk.wrong: Wrong! Come back when you're sharper, Pip.
lines.pointclick.talk.morwen_won: The key's yours, Pip. Off you go.
lines.pointclick.talk.morwen_bye: I'll be here. I always am.
lines.pointclick.talk.ending.1: It's lit! Gull Rock is shining again!
lines.pointclick.talk.ending.2: Steer for the light, all of you. Come home.

lines.pointclick.dock.boat.chained: It's chained to the post. Padlocked, too.
lines.pointclick.dock.boat.oarless: Rowing with my hands would take all night. I need an oar.

notes.pointclick.lamp.log.entry: The lighthouse keeper's last entry in his log, signed with his name (Bram).

notes.pointclick.talk.intro.1: The opening talk: Finn (an old fisherman) to Pip (intro.1, 2, 4 and 5); Pip answers (intro.3).
notes.pointclick.talk.finn_oar.1: Finn, when Pip has the oar already.
notes.pointclick.talk.finn_oar.2: Finn, while the oar is still in the water.
notes.pointclick.talk.finn_key.1: Finn, when Pip has Morwen's key already.
notes.pointclick.talk.finn_key.2: Finn, before Pip has the key.

brief: The point-and-click slice, The Light on Gull Rock: a comic adventure in the manner of Monkey Island, warm and wry. On a fishing harbour at dusk the lighthouse on Gull Rock has gone dark with the fleet out in the fog, and Pip, a young deckhand (a boy: the others call him lad), relights it. Pip speaks most lines, in the first person, describing what the player points at and tries (often with a dry joke); Finn, an old fisherman, Bruno, the tavern keeper (a man), and Morwen, the harbour master (a woman, proud of never losing a riddle contest), talk with him. Morwen's three riddles must work in your language with the same right answers (see their notes). Gull Rock and the Salty Gull (the tavern) are place names you may translate.
